cases.title: Builds the node but never returns it
cases.student_code:
def build_node():
    node = rclpy.create_node('wall_stop')
    publisher = node.create_publisher(Twist, '/cmd_vel', 10)
    node.create_subscription(LaserScan, '/scan', handle_scan, 10)

expected_feedback.diagnosis: build_node() creates the node and its callbacks but ends without returning it, so main() has nothing to spin.
debugging_steps: Read what main() does with the value build_node() gives back.
Find where build_node() ends.
Return the node you created.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: What does main() pass to rclpy.spin(), and where does that value come from?

hint_ladder.hint: main() starts whatever build_node() hands back.
A function without a return statement gives back None.
End build_node() by returning the node you created.

cases.title: Skips infinite readings, so open space looks unusable

expected_feedback.diagnosis: Positive infinity means nothing is in range, but the code discards it like an invalid reading, so with nothing ahead there is no usable distance and the robot never moves.
debugging_steps: Look at what the scan contains when nothing is in front of the robot.
Decide what positive infinity should mean for driving.
Check the open-floor behaviour again.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: When every reading straight ahead is +inf, should the robot drive or stop?
must_mention: positive infinity means nothing in range

hint_ladder.hint: Think about what the lidar reports when nothing is within range.
This assignment follows the ROS convention for +inf, unlike Assignment 6.
Treat +inf as clear instead of filtering it out.

cases.title: Stops while the wall is still far away

expected_feedback.diagnosis: The chosen stop distance is larger than 1.0 m, so the robot stops in a situation where it must still be driving.
debugging_steps: Reread the allowed range for the stop distance.
Compare your constant with that range.
Check which situations require driving.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: If the wall is 1.2 m away, should your robot still be moving?
must_mention: stop distance must be at most 1.0 m

hint_ladder.hint: You choose the stop distance, but within limits.
The robot must still drive when the wall is more than 1.0 m away.
Pick a stop distance between 0.3 m and 1.0 m.

cases.title: Drives near the wall and stops when the way is clear

expected_feedback.diagnosis: The comparison is reversed: the robot drives when the distance is small and stops when it is large.
debugging_steps: Say in words when the robot should stop.
Translate that sentence into a comparison.
Check which branch sets the forward speed.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: Should a smaller distance to the wall make the robot drive or stop?

hint_ladder.hint: Smaller readings mean the wall is closer.
Driving should happen only when the wall is far enough away.
Swap which branch sets the forward speed.

cases.title: Drives for a fixed time instead of reading the scan

expected_feedback.diagnosis: The node decides from elapsed time, so it never reacts to where the wall actually is.
debugging_steps: Find where the code uses scan.ranges.
Identify which reading points straight ahead.
Base the decision on that distance.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: What information tells your node how far away the wall is?

hint_ladder.hint: The wall can be at a different distance every run.
The scan message carries the distances you need.
Use the readings straight ahead to decide.

cases.title: Publishes a turning command

expected_feedback.diagnosis: The command sets angular.z, so the robot turns, but this task requires straight driving.
debugging_steps: List every Twist field your code sets.
Check which field controls turning.
Keep that field at zero.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: Which Twist field makes the robot turn, and should it be zero here?

hint_ladder.hint: The task is to drive straight toward the wall.
Turning comes from one specific Twist field.
Leave angular.z at 0.0 in every command.

cases.title: Rewrites main() instead of writing build_node()

expected_feedback.diagnosis: main() was changed, but the grader relies on the given main() to start every node the same way.
debugging_steps: Compare your main() with the starter code.
Move your setup code into build_node().
Restore main() exactly as given.
expected_feedback.socratic_question: Which function is yours to write, and which one must stay as given?

hint_ladder.hint: The starter splits the work between two functions.
Only build_node() is meant to change.
Put your node setup in build_node() and restore main().
